OLWC_WarcasketHelmet_Overlord.descriptio.english:
Specialized spacer-tech warcasket helmet with standard protection, equipped with signal enhancers that greatly increase the pilot's control bandwidth.

A 10th-generation design from the government program that rebuilt captured pirate rigs around its own power armor and gave them to veterans who could no longer serve any other way. The Overlord was its rig for veteran mechanitors, who would command their own mechs in the field rather than join a squad.

The Overlord series is meant for a mechanitor who goes into battle alone, with only their mechs beside them. The resurrector in the shell holds only a few charges and regains them slowly, so they are best saved for the mechs that matter most. When a fight cannot wait, it can be reloaded with advanced components. The helmet greatly increases the pilot's bandwidth at some cost to their aim, the shoulders carry command relays that reach mechs anywhere on the map, and the arms are left free for smithing and hacking. Because the plating is far tougher than a mechanitor's usual armor, the pilot can lead from the front line rather than from behind the mechs.

OLWC_WarcasketTrait_Overlord.degreeDatas.english: {PAWN_nameDef} is entombed in a warcasket. No amount of pain will have an effect on {PAWN_objective}, and {PAWN_pronoun} can never go into a pain shock or drop unconscious due to pain. Because of how bulky the armor is and how much energy it takes to use it, {PAWN_nameDef} is not capable of most work, but can still do research, smithing and hacking.

OLWC_ResurrectMech.description.english: Resurrect a recently killed mechanoid by externally supercharging its self-repair processes. The mech will come back under the pilot's control with some but not all of its wounds healed, so the pilot needs enough bandwidth for it. Each resurrection costs some of the armor's charges, and heavier mechs cost more.
